entities.evidence: The man who opens the ark’s window is Noah, the flood survivor and son of Lamech. The source tag identifies the same bearer.

review.translation: [And it happened|0] [at the end of|1] [forty|2] [days|3] [that|4] [Noah|5] [opened|4] [the window|7,6] [of the ark|8] [that|9] [he had made|10],

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the time phrase מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם ‘at the end of forty days’. The next clause, וַיִּפְתַּח נֹחַ, gives the event that took place then, ‘Noah opened’ the window.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם places Noah’s opening of the ark’s window at the end of forty days. The duration אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם completes the construct noun קֵץ.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed preposition מִן. Its נ assimilates to the ק, marked by dagesh.

analysis.evidence: In מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, “at the end of forty days,” אַרְבָּעִים counts the days that elapsed before Noah opened the window of the ark.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, “at the end of forty days,” the numeral אַרְבָּעִים counts the days that elapsed before Noah opened the window. Hebrew uses the singular יוֹם here.
נֹחַ is the subject, and אֶת marks חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה (“the window of the ark”) as the direct object. Noah opened the window.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּפְתַּח נֹחַ אֶת חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה, “Noah opened the window of the ark,” נֹחַ names the subject of וַיִּפְתַּח. The ark identifies him as the Noah named in Genesis 5:29.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject of וַיִּפְתַּח ‘opened’. אֶת marks חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה ‘the window of the ark’ as the direct object. The construct phrase is definite because הַתֵּבָה has the article.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּפְתַּח נֹחַ אֶת חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה, Noah opens “the window of the ark.” חַלּוֹן stands in construct with הַתֵּבָה, and אֶת marks the whole phrase as the direct object of וַיִּפְתַּח.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine or feminine, singular construct, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew noun article under its own consonants, תבה.
draft.definition: A container that shelters its occupants on water. In Genesis 8:6 it is Noah’s ark.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:14 directs Noah to build the ark of wood and coat it with pitch. Genesis 7:17–18 describes it afloat, and Genesis 8:6 identifies the window Noah opens as part of it. Exodus 2:3 uses the same noun for the papyrus basket that holds the infant Moses.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 8:6, Noah opens חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה, “the window of the ark.” The article identifies the vessel already described in Genesis 7:17–18, where the rising waters lift it and it floats.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־, with doubling of ת, prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun. The noun completes the construct phrase חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה.
analysis.sense: The vessel that carried Noah, his household, and the animals through the flood.

analysis.evidence: After חַלּוֹן הַתֵּבָה (“the window of the ark”), אֲשֶׁר introduces the relative clause אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (“that he had made”). Noah is the understood subject of עָשָׂה, and the antecedent supplies its object.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: Noah opens the window of the ark. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה describes what he had made before opening the window.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
